elements.label: Live-action footage of two seated men, camera pans right onto the second man

elements.manual_reason: The pixel mosaic over the man's mouth is a small overlay inside the whole-frame diff box b01; no separate candidate covers it.
elements.label: Pixelated censor mosaic over the speaker's mouth

sfx_review.label: other
sfx_review.note: Pure sustained sine tone (single steady band about one second long) starting as the speaker cuts off on 'for...'; a comedic censor bleep paired with the mouth mosaic, not a chime.

pattern.description: In live-action footage the camera pans right onto a man as he starts to say something; a pixel mosaic pops over his mouth and a sustained sine bleep covers the line.
pattern.why_premium: A deliberate TV-style censor gag (mosaic plus bleep synced to the cut-off word) lands a joke without dialogue, giving a scripted ad a human, self-aware tone.

build_hint.gsap: Footage layer: gsap.fromTo('.footage', {xPercent: 0}, {xPercent: -8, duration: 0.8, ease: 'power1.inOut'}); mosaic: gsap.set('.mosaic', {autoAlpha: 1}) at the bleep start (a pixelate filter tracked to the mouth), hold for the bleep duration, then gsap.set autoAlpha 0.
build_hint.remotion: Footage translateX = interpolate(frame, [0, 24], [0, -8], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'})%; mosaic = <Sequence from={bleepStart} durationInFrames={bleepLen}> with a pixelated crop of the mouth region; bleep = <Audio> of a 1 kHz sine for the same span.

notes: Camera verdict is pan_right (real camera move in footage). The mosaic appears from about f201 onward in the filmstrip; its manual box is approximate. Taxonomy sfx has no 'bleep'/'censor' label, so x001 is 'other'; may be worth a taxonomy proposal.
